=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/consumer_health_check.sh:final `write_failures` block (`if tg_send_msg ... && [ -n "${GITHUB_OUTPUT:-}" ]`) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `failure_alerted=true` is written whenever `tg_send_msg` exits 0, even if nothing was delivered. The helper returns 0 on level filter (line 114), missing secret or chat id (line 121) and curl failure (line 129), and `>/dev/null` discards the id.
  WHY: After a transient failure the daily alert cache is saved, and no page is sent for the rest of the UTC day. Suggested fix: capture `msg_id="$(tg_send_msg "${alert}" "WARNING" || true)"` and write the output only when it is non-empty.
- scripts/consumer_health_check.py:`newest = _parse_time(str(run0.get("run_started_at") or run0.get("created_at") or ""))` | severity=NIT | confidence=1
  PROBLEM: The `created_at` fallback can mask a silent poller if `run_started_at` is missing.
  WHY: The API always sets `run_started_at`, so the fallback is only reached for malformed data. The reviewer did not report it as a defect.

A comment explains that "Stage workflow support files" deletes `.codex-workflow-src-main` earlier, so a fallback could never run. This is stale PR-description wording. | severity=NIT | confidence=2

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- scripts/consumer_health_check.sh:270 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The once-a-day failure page is marked as sent (`failure_alerted=true`) even when no Telegram message was delivered. `tg_send_msg` (scripts/tg_helpers.sh:108-134) always returns 0 (level filter at line 114, missing credentials at line 121, curl failure at line 129), and the code discards its output with `>/dev/null`.
  WHY: When Telegram is down, misconfigured or filtered, `failure_alerted=true` is still written and the cache entry is saved. Every later retry that UTC day skips the alert, so no operator is paged.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- scripts/consumer_health_check.sh:268-273 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `tg_send_msg` (scripts/tg_helpers.sh:108-134) returns 0 on the level filter (line 113-114), on missing `TG_BOT_SECRET` or chat id (line 120-121) and on curl failure (line 127-129). `>/dev/null` discards the id, and the `&&` only tests `GITHUB_OUTPUT`, so `failure_alerted=true` is written without a delivered message.
  WHY: A transient failure on the first failing tick saves the daily cache entry, and later retries that UTC day skip the page. The repo convention (`STANDALONE_CONFLICT_STUCK` in orchestrate_poll_process.sh) records the alerted marker only after Telegram returns a message id.
- scripts/consumer_health_check.py:103-106 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: When the newest poll run has no `run_started_at` (a queued run that has not started), the code falls back to `created_at`. That counts a run that never started as poller activity and contradicts the README signal and the code's own comment.
  WHY: With a low `CONSUMER_HEALTH_POLLER_SILENT_HOURS` or a GitHub queue wedge, `created_at` masks the silence, `poller_silent` is omitted and an existing issue can be closed. This only fires when `run_started_at` is null.
- tests/test_consumer_health_check.py:`test_the_script_opens_enables_and_closes` / `test_a_failed_read_of_this_repos_issues_fails_the_day` vs. scripts/consumer_health_check.sh lines 258-275 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The once-a-day failure WARNING path has no behavioural test. Coverage is limited to workflow-wiring string assertions.
  WHY: A behavioural test would have exercised the `tg_send_msg`-returns-0-on-failure path, so the suppression contract is untested.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
